Title: Contact Us page loads and displays contact details
Preconditions: Streamlit dependency installed and app not already running on chosen port
Steps: 1. Run 'streamlit run ui/app.py' | 2. Wait for the local URL to be printed | 3. Open the local URL in a browser
Expected Result: The 'Contact Us' page renders with title 'Contact Us', a Name field showing 'Radhika', and a Phone Number field showing '87382782'

Title: User navigates to app URL and views full Contact Us page end-to-end
Preconditions: App server started with 'streamlit run ui/app.py'
Steps: 1. Start the app | 2. Open browser to the printed Local URL | 3. Observe the page title in browser tab | 4. Read the displayed Name and Phone Number values
Expected Result: Browser tab title/page shows 'Contact Us', and both the Name ('Radhika') and Phone Number ('87382782') fields are visible and correctly populated end-to-end

Title: App handles being loaded on a non-default port without errors
Preconditions: Port 8501 (default) is occupied by another process
Steps: 1. Start app with an alternate port, e.g. 'streamlit run ui/app.py --server.port 8765' | 2. Request the app URL | 3. Verify response
Expected Result: App starts successfully on the alternate port and returns HTTP 200 with the Contact Us page content

Title: Displayed Name and Phone Number fields are read-only and match provided values exactly
Steps: 1. Open the Contact Us page | 2. Attempt to click into the Name field | 3. Attempt to click into the Phone Number field | 4. Attempt to type into each field
Expected Result: Both fields are disabled/read-only, cannot be edited, and continue to display the exact values 'Radhika' and '87382782'

Title: Missing streamlit dependency prevents app from starting with a clear error
Preconditions: streamlit package is NOT installed in the active Python environment
Steps: 1. Uninstall or use an environment without streamlit | 2. Run 'streamlit run ui/app.py' | 3. Observe the command output
Expected Result: Command fails with a 'streamlit' not found / ModuleNotFoundError style message rather than a silent failure or crash with an unrelated stack trace
